newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia pledges to arrest more paedophiles.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia pledges to arrest more paedophiles.

text.p: Cambodian police on Thursday pledged to crack down on foreign paedophiles, drawing praise and encouragement from children's rights workers who have complained of past police inaction on child sex abuse.

"Believe me, we will arrest more. They are here in town," Cambodia Interpol chief General Skadavy M. Ly Roun told reporters after presenting a 53-year-old Canadian national accused of having sex with children.

"This seems to be the first initiative when Cambodian police have taken action against foreigners (suspected of child sex offences)," Tim Seaman of the human-rights group LICADHO told Reuters. "It's a very positive step."
The police vow was especially heartening to children's rights activists because they believed the country's top leaders were behind it.
Co-premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh on Tuesday strongly condemned foreigners who visit Cambodia for sex with children and said they should be punished severely.
The handcuffed Canadian suspect, who was arrested at a Phnom Penh guest house on Tuesday, complained about his treatment during his brief appearance.
"I haven't seen any charges," he said.
Skadavy M. Ly Roun said he planned to present the Canadian before the Phnom Penh Municipal Court on Thursday afternoon, which could result in formal charges being filed.
Police last week arrested Frenchman Amedee Hennion, 54, who has since been charged by prosecutors with child sex offences.
Child welfare groups have long warned that Cambodia has become a haven for local and foreign paedophiles, but there have been few arrests on child sex charges.

An Austrian was fined and deported in June 1995 and a Briton was fined and jailed for five months in October 1995. Seaman said the earlier arrests were initiated by non-governmental organisations but Cambodian police had begun to take action.
"We will be encouraging them to continue," Seaman said.
